mods.name: RadioCraft
mods.description:
Radiocraft is a Minecraft mod that adds ham radio (also known as Amateur Radio) into Minecraft Java edition.

* Adds realistic, immersive communication
*Survival-friendly, challenging, and satisfying functionality
* Educational and accurate (albeit simplified) representations of the real ham radio hobby!

What is Ham Radio?

Ham radio is a hobby and service that involves using the radio frequency spectrum for various purposes, such as communication, experimentation, education, and emergency assistance. Ham radio operators, also known as amateur radio operators or hams, need to obtain a license from their government to operate on certain frequency bands and follow certain rules. Ham radio allows hams to talk to other hams across the world, or even into space, using different modes of transmission, such as voice, text, image, and data. Ham radio is also a way to meet new people, learn new skills, and have fun!

# RadioCraft alpha 1.13

Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge. Needs Simple Voice Chat and GeckoLib;
[Another Weather Mod](https://github.com/RadiocraftARRL/AnotherWeatherMod) is optional (1.13.0 or later).
Everything below is explained in the in-game ARRL Radiocraft Handbook and on the [wiki](https://radiocraft.bigtimeradio.us/wiki/).

## 1.13.1

### Fixed
- The FIRE ALARM, SCADA and FCC Monitor program floppies can now be crafted (they were creative-only in 1.13.0), each
  a blank floppy and one more item, shapeless:
  - **FIRE ALARM**: flint and steel.
  - **SCADA**: a redstone repeater.
  - **FCC Monitor**: a spyglass.

## 1.13.0

### New

#### Every HF band has its own job
- Skip now follows real typical ranges, at 2 blocks a kilometre, and each band is good for something different:
  - **80m** is the regional band: line of sight 800 blocks, skip 100-1,000 by day and 100-4,000 at night. Its skip
    starts inside its line of sight, so it has **no silent zone**.
  - **40m** is the daytime workhorse: line of sight 650, skip 100-2,000 by day. At night it **goes long**
    (2,000-7,000) and loses the middle distances to 80m.
  - **20m** is for distance by day: line of sight 500, skip 1,600-8,000 by day and 3,000-8,000 at night, but weak at
    night in average and fair weather and closed in poor.
  - **10m** reaches a little further locally than 40m (line of sight 700). In **average** solar weather it now opens
    lightly by day, reaching only the near part of its skip window (2,500-3,490 blocks); in good and great weather it
    opens fully. At night it stays closed except in great weather.
  - **CB** follows 10m: line of sight 525, a light daytime opening of 1,750-2,440 blocks in average weather, full when
    the sun is lively, and no night skip. **Low band** has a line of sight of 600.
- Which band for which distance: up to 1,000 blocks, 80 or 40m by day and 80m at night; to 2,000, 40m by day and 80m
  at night; to 4,000, 20m by day and 40 or 80m at night; further, 20m by day and 40m at night. The Handbook's Bands &
  Range entry has the whole picture.
- **Radio horizon**: line of sight reaches further from high ground. A band's range grows with the square root of each
  antenna's height above the average terrain around it. Two masts 6 blocks above the land round them get the band's
  usual range; a hilltop or a tall tower gets much more (up to 8 times); two handhelds on flat ground get about half.
- **Takeoff angle per hop**: each skip hop leaves at the angle that reaches the sky half way along it, on a curved
  earth. A short 80m hop goes nearly straight up and the longest hops skim the horizon at about 3 degrees. A station
  deep in a valley loses long, low hops over the valley walls but keeps short, steep ones. Stations now look 256
  blocks out for what blocks a low angle (it was 64).
- **Multi-hop skip** on 10m, 20m and 40m (and CB and low band with 10m): while the band is fair or better and fully
  open, a signal can bounce off the ground and up again, up to 3 hops. Two hops reach twice as far and three hops
  three times; each hop past the first leaves about half the signal.
- **Sunrise and sunset**: bands no longer snap from day to night. While the sun is near the horizon (about 1,900 ticks)
  each band's skip window slides from its night place to its day one, a band that skips only by day fades in and out,
  and the solar weather's day and night conditions blend the same way.
- An antenna's **skip scale** (verticals, the 5-BTV, the CB whip) now moves the whole skip window out, silent zone and
  all, not only its far edge.
- Live radios, the Propagation Predictor (PREDICT) and `/bandcalculate` all use these rules. PREDICT stays hourly.

#### Satellites
- A **satellite** is an FM repeater in orbit. During a pass, anyone with open sky can work it from thousands of blocks
  away: talk on its **uplink** with its tone, and it sends you out on its **downlink** to everyone under it. It passes

releases.notes:
**RadioCraft 1.12.0 is out!**  This might be our biggest release yet. Thanks for your patience on this one. I kept adding in more features and it took a bit of work to get it playing nicely.

### New radios
We recently decided to add some more bands/radio types. In this update we're adding CB radios and commercial radios. Some people might not love that we're adding CBs, but I wanted to highlight the difference between the radios that need licenses and those that don't (and why it's worth the licenses). CBs aren't great but they're a great fun place to start! Additionally, this is *Radiocraft* not *Ham Radio Craft*. The radio hobby works closely alongside the other bands and its all similar tech, so we want to have a place for it. Ham radio will always be the main focus. We also plan to add dedicated vhf air band (AM) and broadcast radio.

- **CB radio**: a TRC-217-style portable (this was a model I had and adored as a kid) and two mobiles (the 5875 with SSB, clarifier and a clock; the PC68), all 40 channels, no licence prompt. Plus a CB ground plane antenna.
- **Commercial radios** (handhelds, mobiles, repeaters, digital voice) and
- **Marine radios** with weather channels and DSC distress (received on the radio computer if a marine radio is connected).
- **Personal Distress Beacon** - one time use vhf distress beacon (separate from the DSC). Computers can receive if they have a commercial radio attached (in the same distress app as DC). We plan to have DSC and personal distress beacons repeat from satellites once we figure out how we want to do those.
- **New HF panels** for the 10m, 20m, 40m, 80m and all-band radios, and the VHF base station: real meters, AGC, squelch, AM, QUICK recall, 10X tuning. The all-band radio has 50 memories. The old textures were great, but didn't perfectly match the models and had some textures I updated, while staying true to the inspiration.

### The radio computer
- A whole desktop: logbook, awards, QSL cards, APRS, RTTY, FT8, packet BBS, SSTV and fax, the propagation forecast, a repeater directory and more. I'm really happy with the icons, especially.
- **Rig Control** with a live waterfall, scanning, and **remote control of a rig** by connecting to another computer which has a radio using a wire and/or microwave link, audio and all.

### How radio works
- SSB, AM and FM now hear each other as they really would. SSB is only there while someone talks, so the S-meter and squelch follow the voice.
- Squelch, noise blankers, AGC and coax/grounding all matter. Grounding lowers noise; a lightning arrestor saves the station from strikes.
- Repeaters that hear each other lock up with a feedback howl (or not: there's a server setting). They MIGHT have crashed the server before :grimacing: 

## Also new
- A film camera (for sstv),
- ADS-B for Sable aircraft
- weather alerts, FCC field gear (just decorative, admin only for now), advancements, the Real-World Interface, power switches, an emergency chemical battery, alkaline cells, junction boxes for data wire, and the guide book is now the **ARRL Radiocraft Handbook** to honor those that funded the project.
- `/contest start` and `/contest stop` - lets admins run a radio contest and track all sorts of metrics that they get in a book for server-hosted contests.

releases.notes:
# RadioCraft alpha 1.11

Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge. Needs Simple Voice Chat and GeckoLib;
[Another Weather Mod](https://github.com/RadiocraftARRL/AnotherWeatherMod) is optional.
Everything below is explained in the in-game guide and on the [wiki](https://radiocraft.bigtimeradio.us/wiki/).

## 1.11.0

### New

- **Handheld memory channels**: hold MW to store, tap MW to switch; channels can have 7-letter names.
- **APRS module** for the handheld: nearby stations with a compass, messages, and a position beacon.
- **DTMF**: # on the handheld sends tones; new DTMF Encoder and Decoder blocks (codes to redstone).
- **Repeater Autopatch Controller**: phone calls through a repeater by DTMF.
- **Field phone** (party line on data wire), **Phone PA**, and linked PABXes with All-Call.
- **Radio Moderation Computer** (admins only): live listening (to a player, or to everything on a frequency),
  recording archive, map, and who-hears-whom, with sortable lists and a Freeze for the live view. It stays where you
  left it for a while and shows its screen on its monitor. Recording is off by default (server config).
- **Scroll tuning**: sneak and scroll while looking at a radio (can be turned off in the client config).
- Dyed data wire, and new sounds (H19, power buttons, FM static).

### Changes

- **Handheld**: new LCD screen, and a 3D model in hand, on the belt and in the charger, with a live screen.
- **Desk charger**: the radio keeps working in it, it takes power wire, sneak-use docks the radio, charging is slower.
- Radios can't hear while transmitting (repeaters excepted).
- 3D hand microphone.
- PABX numbering and naming reworked; phones draw power through the PABX.
- More realistic SSB mixing and static; nearby transmitters desense receivers.
- WEFAX bulletins are real fax audio; local HF works at half range in a blackout.
- Signals pass through wood, glass, wool and leaves.
- Better antenna analyzer readout, `/solarweather` controls, tooltips on everything.
- The Config button in the mod list is back, with readable names for every setting.
- The handheld volume knob turns down more naturally; the direction finder's beep is quieter.

### Fixes

- A shorted power wire no longer keeps burning after it is replaced.
- Antenna analyzer crash, tower beacons not blinking, desk charger tooltip.

releases.notes:
# RadioCraft alpha 1.10.0

Everything since 1.9.2, including 1.9.3's config fix (1.9.3 was never published). Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge. Needs
Simple Voice Chat; [Another Weather Mod](https://github.com/RadiocraftARRL/AnotherWeatherMod) 1.10.0 is optional and
adds live storms, tornado watches and day outlooks to the weather reports and WEFAX charts.

## Changes that affect existing worlds

- **Every telephone needs a Phone PABX now.** A microwave radio is no longer a phone exchange on its own: phones that
  were wired straight to a microwave radio say NO LINE until a powered PABX joins them (see Telephones below).
- **Plain wire only carries power.** Teletypes, faxes, WEFAX receivers, radio interfaces, the tape player, the
  Ionospheric Processor, wired speakers and microwave stations that do not touch their radio now link over the new
  data wire. Rewire them with data wire.

## Telephones

- **Phone PABX**, the exchange every phone needs: phones touching it or on its data wire call each other by
  extension. It needs power (`pabx_power_use`, 2 a tick) and its lamp shows green when it has it.
- Right click a PABX to set its **master number**, its **first extension** (its phones are numbered from it, 100 by
  default) and whether it is **behind another PABX**.
- PABXes on a microwave link (touching a radio, or on its data wire) are dialed by master number then extension: with
  master number 602, extension 100 is `602100`. A PABX behind another works like one of its lines, its number dialed
  before the extension, so you can build a whole phone network.
- The phone shows its full number and who is calling; the call timer now counts (it stuck at 0:00).
- Telephones have their own guide chapter, with a tip on Simple Voice Chat: with push-to-talk, hold its key while you
  speak on a phone; open mic never keys a radio.

## Wiring and antennas

- **Data wire**: a light grey wire for the station's data and audio lines (see above).
- **Antenna switch**: one radio to one of three antennas. Its input turns to the radio's coax by itself; a knob picks
  the output.
- **Receive-only antenna splitter**: every radio behind it hears the antenna, a little weaker; none can transmit
  through it. Recipe: four coax round an iron ingot.
- A radio on a dummy load plays only a faint hiss.

## Weather

- **WEFAX alarms**: the receiver gives a redstone signal, 1 for a message, 2 for a severe thunderstorm, 3 for a
  tornado watch and 4 for a hurricane (the strongest alert wins), and beeps.
- Tornado watches and today's and tomorrow's outlook from Another Weather Mod on the WEFAX and in weather reports.
- Lightning breaks the handhelds and manpacks a struck player carries (`lightning_breaks_carried_radios`), and a
  manpack hurts more (`lightning_manpack_extra_damage`).

## Sound

- Two stations on one frequency now mix: SSB adds them, FM captures the stronger and flips between them when they are
  close. Received levels glide instead of jumping (`voice_level_smoothing`).
- The redstone interference noise no longer goes off near Another Weather Mod's weather instruments in a storm (their
  readings are not switching), follows the radio's volume knob, and fades with distance like the static. The
  teletype and WEFAX chatter fade with distance too.

## Fixes and looks

- `radiocraft-server.toml` no longer corrects itself on every load, and edited band frequencies stay
  ([issue #102](https://github.com/RadiocraftARRL/RadioCraft/issues/102)).
- The radio fax's case uses its wood's planks.
- The HF manpack screen no longer overlaps; its battery reading sits at the right of the window.
- Breaking a WEFAX receiver (or a lit charge controller) shows its own particles, not the missing-texture ones.
- The antenna switch knob no longer flickers.
- Guide builds face their gear toward you, draw their antenna wires, and gain a microwave site.

# RadioCraft alpha 1.9.2

A fix for 1.9.1, which could not start at all: the game stopped with `Failed to load mod file
META-INF/jarjar/sable-companion-common-1.21.1-1.6.0.jar`. The build step that fixed 1.9.0's JOrbis crash also unpacked
the bundled Sable Companion library, so the jar named a file it no longer had. The library is bundled intact again.
Sable stays optional; RadioCraft starts without it. Every release is now launched on a real NeoForge server and client
before it is published. Nothing else changed.

# RadioCraft alpha 1.9.0

Everything since the 1.2.0 release (commit 1476893, 2026-10-21). Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge. Needs Simple Voice
Chat; [Another Weather Mod](https://github.com/ITCMD/AnotherWeatherMod) 1.9.0 is optional and adds live storms to the
weather reports and WEFAX charts.

## Radios

- Each radio's frequency, mode and S-meter show on its model's screen (hidable in the client config), and the gain
  and mic gain dials work.
- The desk microphone works: hold to talk, sneak-click to lock, quieter with distance, with a timeout. Sneak-right-
  click a radio to take its hand mic on a cord; walk away and it snaps back.
- CW from the keyboard (Left Alt, rebindable) and from Chat Morse.
- Desk speakers, the wall speaker and the loudspeaker play the radio's audio; floor cables are drawn between radios
  and the accessories beside them.
- The HF manpack, worn on the back: a QRP whip, SSB and CW. The VHF handheld goes on the Curios belt with a talk key
  and drains its battery over days.
- FM receivers hiss under a weak signal and are silent otherwise.
- A bad SWR blows a radio's transmitter and poor-crystal radios can explode.
- Callsigns: choose your own real-format ham callsign, or let the game pick one, the first time you reach for a
  radio (`/callsign claim`). Repeaters get X#XX callsigns by distance from spawn. Operator moderation with
  `/radio moderateall` and `/radio moderate <player>`.

## Antennas and matching

- New antennas: delta loop, Moxon, the Hustler 5-BTV multiband vertical, the VHF Ringo, the 2-bay folded dipole
  (found at sites) and the ionosonde antenna.
- The antenna tuner is a real manual tuner with three dials and a tuning lamp. The new automatic tuner tunes itself
  on a band change and gives up with TUNE FAIL past its range.
- The duplexer's six cavity screws tune its TX and RX cavities; a badly tuned duplexer desenses its repeater. Coax
  behind a repeater runs up into its duplexer, and tuners join a radio by touching.
- Lightning: antennas draw strikes, lightning rods work as VHF antennas, and a strike blows the radios on an
  antenna, burns its coax and can light the batteries.
- `/bandcalculate <from> <to>` lists every band between two points, counting terrain losses.

## Propagation and solar weather

- Terrain-aware propagation: hills block line of sight, cliffs cost HF, valley walls cut low-angle skip, handhelds
  are weaker indoors. The terrain map is saved with the world and refreshed as chunks change.
- Sporadic E opens VHF for long range in good conditions, 10m has a long single-hop skip zone, and the aurora can
  appear at any Z.
- Propagation scaling for large servers: receivers out of any possible reach are skipped with one distance check,
  and fixed stations keep their terrain result until a chunk on the path changes.
- The solar weather station became the Teletype Machine: a 400-line roll that prints the solar report and RTTY at
  6 characters a second with real teletype sounds, collisions and per-line moderation. The Ionosonde and the
  Ionospheric Processor measure conditions for it.

## Power

- The large battery takes and gives Forge Energy, so Create water wheels and other mods' generators charge it; with
  Create installed, RadioCraft adds an alternator. Power is balanced around a large water wheel.
- The charge controller switch works; the repeater, the H19 terminal and the automatic tuner draw power.
- Power wire is now thin and comes in sixteen colours; coax is dyeable too. Wire bundles carry up to seven cables
  in one block, keeping their order round bends and up tower legs. The Wire Junction joins power wire of any colour.
- Hazards: a closed loop of power wire shorts and burns through, wet plain wire electrocutes, an open end in the
  rain sparks, and large batteries catch fire from flame, lava, a flint and steel or lightning. Four or more
  burning together explode. Server config `Battery Fires`.

Radiocraft is a Minecraft mod that adds ham radio (also known as Amateur Radio) into Minecraft Java edition.

* Adds realistic, immersive communication
*Survival-friendly, challenging, and satisfying functionality
* Educational and accurate (albeit simplified) representations of the real ham radio hobby!

What is Ham Radio?

Ham radio is a hobby and service that involves using the radio frequency spectrum for various purposes, such as communication, experimentation, education, and emergency assistance. Ham radio operators, also known as amateur radio operators or hams, need to obtain a license from their government to operate on certain frequency bands and follow certain rules. Ham radio allows hams to talk to other hams across the world, or even into space, using different modes of transmission, such as voice, text, image, and data. Ham radio is also a way to meet new people, learn new skills, and have fun!
